To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
large conductance calcium-dependent potassium channels contribute to action potential repolariation in cerebellar purkinje neurons and that they control intracellular calcium entry with each spike.

large conductance calcium activated potassium channels contribute to the afterhyperpolarizations that follow action potentials, that the contribution of BK to the AHP decreases with age, and that the BK dependent AHP is important for regulating intracellular calcium concentrations in Purkinje neurons.
large conductance calcium activated potassium channels affect both the firing pattern and the intracellular calcium concentration of cerebellar purkinje neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BK channels in the control of the firing pattern of cerebellar neurons.
the role of BK channels in the regulation of spontaneous firing in Purkinje neurons and how this role changes with age.
the functional contribution of BK channels in Purkinje neurons and the effect of age on the function of BK channels in this neuronal population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BK channels are involved in controlling the firing rate of Purkinje cells and the intracellular calcium level in the Purkinje cells.
BK channels contribute to the AHP in Purkinje neurons, and that this contribution is age dependent.
BK channels are not involved in action potential repolarisation, but are involved in controlling the intracellular Ca2+ concentration during the action potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BK channels contribute to the firing pattern of cerebellar neurons by regulating the AHP and calcium influx.
BK channels contribute to the control of Purkinje cell firing and calcium concentration in a way that is dependent on the pattern of firing and age of the animal.
the role of BK channels in the Purkinje neuron is to control the frequency of firing and the intracellular calcium concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BK channels contribute to the AHP and control calcium entry with every action potential, but they do not contribute significantly to action potential reporlarization.
BK channel block has different effects depending on the pattern of activity of the Purkinje neuron.
BK channels have a significant effect on Purkinje cell firing in vivo, and this effect is dependent on the firing mode.
